GAP [1]: The mechanism by which the AcCoA-NLRX1 axis regulates mitophagy response to KRAS inhibitors is unknown, and understanding this process is crucial for developing strategies to overcome KRAS inhibitor resistance.
GAP [2]: No study has tested whether USP7 interacts with the KRAS signaling pathway under conditions of KRAS G12C inhibition, which is necessary to understand the role of USP7 in KRAS inhibitor resistance.
GAP [3]: It is unclear whether the KRAS-MYC axis acts upstream or downstream of the mitophagy response in KRAS-mutant tumors, and elucidating this relationship is essential for identifying potential therapeutic targets.
GAP [4]: The causal path from KRAS G12C inhibitors to drug resistance through the KRAS signaling pathways is missing experimental validation of the intermediate steps, which is necessary to understand the mechanisms of resistance and develop effective combination therapies.
GAP [5]: The mechanism by which redundancies within the KRAS signaling pathways contribute to KRAS inhibitor resistance is unknown, and understanding this process is critical for developing strategies to target these redundant pathways and improve treatment outcomes.
